## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Maccharājacariya* ("The Conduct of the Fish-king") is the thirtieth narrative (Cp 30) of the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, located in the late sutta section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral; Bareau n.d.]. It illustrates the Bodhisatta's fulfillment of the perfection of truthfulness (*sacca-pāramitā*) [Bareau n.d.]. In this story, the Bodhisatta is reborn as a king of fish dwelling in a large pond; when the water dries up under the intense heat of the summer sun, predatory birds—such as crows, vultures, herons, hawks, and eagles—begin devouring the exposed fish, prompting the Bodhisatta's act of truth [Bareau n.d.].

In terms of textual reuse and commentary, DharmaNexus identifies 12 matching passages between the text and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match at §8.1–8.4), reflecting the commentary's incorporation and explanation of the canonical verses [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato available on SuttaCentral, as well as a French translation and comparative study by André Bareau [SuttaCentral; Bareau n.d.].
